status_rationale: Gate C is approved and Lean mapping v7 exists at Spec2Lean.PTX.OrB32. This second revision replaces obligations-v1 with a smaller, clearer set of obligations and tighter traceability for theorem-strength review; no proofs are written.

unit.bounded_unit: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded unit `or.b32 d, a, b;` with optional predication
unit.scope_boundary: Only .b32 with optional predication is formalized. Destination/source2 are local bounded model types; source-1 is register-only by architecture restriction; no malformed/exception behavior is added.

compliance_notes: No proofs are included in this stage.
No semantics are imported from unrelated units.

No vacuous determinism claims: relational determinism is phrased over the inductive relation OrB32Step (not function single-valuedness), and correspondence obligations explicitly cover the partial none-case in execOrB32.
Theorems with `_` destination use only architecture-design strength (D-2 + D-6 + AMB-OR-2) and explicitly record this as a strength caveat, not a source-specific or-b32-only claim.

validation_obligations.title: Bounded instruction shape and ordering
validation_obligations.description: OrB32Instruction has fields (guard, d, a, b) with a: Source1 register-only and b: Source2 reg/imm, matching bounded-or syntax and architecture restriction.

validation_obligations.title: 32-bit value and minimal state representation
validation_obligations.description: B32 is Fin (2^32); MachineState contains exactly valueRegs and predRegs, with partial lookup via Option.

validation_obligations.title: No prohibited verification bypasses
validation_obligations.description: OrB32-v7.lean introduces no sorry/admit/axiom/unsafe constructs in the Lean declarations used by this unit.

theorem_obligations.intent: For fixed state and instruction, the relation OrB32Step yields at most one post-state.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If OrB32Step s i s1 and OrB32Step s i s2, then s1 = s2.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32Step_deterministic (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState) (h1 : OrB32Step s i s1) (h2 : OrB32Step s i s2) : s1 = s2
strength_risks: Non-vacuity relies on the relation having both constructors (notExecuted and executed); this is a Prop relation, not a function single-valuedness fact.
Proof must keep constructors disjoint by evaluating guard outcome equality (some false vs some true).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation is inhabited on concrete example states (e.g., unguarded instruction with resolvable sources), so equality of post-states is meaningful and not a trivial definitionality property.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case split on h1 and h2; same constructor gives reflexive equality or reduces to equal `updateDestination`; constructor mismatch contradicts evalGuard equality (false vs true).

theorem_obligations.intent: Show execOrB32 and OrB32Step are equivalent on complete outcomes and agree on partiality (none).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) executed outcome implies step; (b) notExecuted outcome implies step; (c) any step yields either an executed or notExecuted function outcome; (d) execOrB32 = none iff no step exists.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem execOrB32_executed_sound : ... ; theorem execOrB32_notExecuted_sound : ... ; theorem OrB32Step_complete : ... ; theorem execOrB32_none_iff_no_step : ...
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Mutual correspondence and partial-equivalence between the executable and relational semantics.
strength_risks: Must avoid strengthening to totality: none is intentional partiality for missing inputs/undefined reads per design and OQ-2/AMB-OR2 context.
No exception/recovery behavior is to be inferred from this obligation.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both directions are substantive: `some` branches and `none` branch can be realized from concrete states, so equivalence cannot collapse to a tautology.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execOrB32 and OrB32Step; split on evalGuard and source reads for each direction. For part (d), forward: from no constructor in relation derive impossible branches for execOrB32 = some. Reverse: any step constructor forbids function none by definitional unfolding.

theorem_obligations.intent: When guard is true and both sources resolve, executed post-state writes bitwise OR result into destination register.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For destination register r, if evalGuard is true and reads resolve to va and vb, then execOrB32 returns an executed post-state where r now contains orValue va vb.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem execOrB32_or_result_fidelity (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va vb : B32) (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) (ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va) (hb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb) : ∃ s', execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (orValue va vb)
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va
hb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb
theorem_obligations.conclusion: ∃ s', execOrB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') ∧ s'.valueRegs r = some (orValue va vb)
strength_risks: Statement excludes partiality paths; requires explicit hguard and source-read hypotheses to avoid strengthening beyond approved scope.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The conclusion pins a concrete value-level equation; it distinguishes OR semantics from any other destination write and therefore is substantive.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Use hguard, ha, hb to select the executed branch of execOrB32; rewrite hd and evaluate updateDestination at Destination.reg r.

theorem_obligations.intent: Bit-bucket destination does not change any state in the bounded model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For any step OrB32Step s i s' with i.d = Destination.bitBucket, the post-state equals the pre-state.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32Step_bitBucket_noop (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket) : s' = s
strength_risks: Bit-bucket support is a bounded architecture/design inference (general PTX syntax rule), not a unit-specific source assertion in PTX-9.3-OR-005; this is an explicit strength caveat.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The mapping defines a separate Destination.bitBucket constructor and branch in updateDestination; this theorem checks that branch at the relational level, so it is not a vacuous shape claim.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Split on h. In the executed constructor, use hd to rewrite Destination.bitBucket and simplify updateDestination; in notExecuted case, conclusion is immediate by constructor form.

theorem_obligations.intent: Executed steps do not modify predicate state in the bounded model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: If an executed step relates s to s' (or equivalently execOrB32 returns executed), then predicate registers are unchanged pointwise.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch: theorem OrB32Step_preserves_predicates_on_executed (s : MachineState) (i : OrB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (va vb : B32) (h : OrB32Step s i s') (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true) (ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va) (hb : readSource2 s i.b = some vb) : ∀ p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true
ha : readSource1 s i.a = some va
hb : readSource2 s i b = some vb
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The bounded state includes predicate registers, and updateDestination only changes valueRegs; theorem ensures predicate frame property is preserved under the executed case rather than assumed vacuously.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on h; the executed constructor updates only via updateDestination, whose record update rewrites valueRegs only. PredRegs fields are definitional equal in s' and s.
